rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE ROLE OF PARENTS ASSOCIATIONS, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE NATIONAL PARENT COUNCIL AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: One of the objectives of this bill is to affirm the right and duty of parents to organize themselves and form associations for the purpose of expressing their ideas on the proper and effective education of their children.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: chge of ctte. ref'l from Gov't Reog. as per J.17; p.14(Aug. 28,2001)

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING INCENTIVES FOR COMMUNITY NEWSPAPERS WITH AN EDUCATIONAL THRUST, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The proposed measure aims to provide government support and incentives to encourage the establishment of a community newspaper in every municipality, city or province published primarily for curriculum enrichment, national integration and unity, andthe fostering of national conciousness and desirable values.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL HEALTH CODE OF 2001
rows.abstract: This proposed Code seeks to unify the health care delivery system by emphasizing the meaningful partnership each health component - the government units, the private sector, the nongovernment units and the community should perform to make health care available, accessible, acceptable and affordable to the individual.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C065
rows.title_full: AN ACT REDUCING THE WATER RATES AND CHARGES FOR WATER USERS IN THE BARANGAY HOSTING THE WATER SOURCE WITHIN A WATER DISTRICT THEREBY AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 198, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Reducing the Water Rates and Charges for Water Users in the Barangay Hosting the Water Source
rows.abstract: Sec. 37, chapter IX, Title II of Presidential Decree No. 198 as amended, is hereby further amended to read as follows: "Sec. 37. Rates and Charges. - Water-A district may sell water under its control, under schedules of rates and charges as may be determined by the Board, to any and all water users within the district [.]: PROVIDED, THAT SUCH RATES AND CHARGES APPLICABLE TO THE      WATER USERS IN THE BARANGAYS HOSTING THE WATER SOURCE SHALL BE 20% LOWER THAN THE RATES AND CHARGES APPLICABLE TOTHE OTHER WATER USERS WITHIN THE DISTRICTS.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-09-03, transmitted to on 2002-09-03 and received by the Senate on 2002-09-03

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: C065
rows.mother_status: Printed copies distributed to members on 2004-05-24
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SCHOOL OF AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF STO. DOMINGO, PROVINCE OF ALBAY TO BE KNOWN AS THE STO. DOMINGO AGRO-FISHERIES POLYTECHNIC, AND AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Substituted by HB06692

rows.author: C065
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MODERNIZATION OF THE SCHOOL HEALTH AND NUTRITION PROGRAM (SHNP) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION, CULTURE AND SPORTS, AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill is premised on the policy of the State to pursue the following objectives: (1)  the development of an efficient and effective health care delivery system in the schools; (2) the development, evaluation and application of appropriate methods and procedures in preventive health care; (3)  the development of reforms in the management of human and material resources.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: chnge of cttee. ref'l from Basic Ed and Cultulre, Higher and Technical Ed and Appropriat ions as per

rows.author: C065
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 26, CHAPTER 4, BOOK VI OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987"
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to AMEND Section 26 of the Administrative Code of 1987 (EO No. 292) to read as follows: All expenditures for (1) personnel retirement premiums, government service insurace, and other similar fixed SOCIAL SECURITY expenditures [, (2)principal and interest on public debt, (3) national govenment guarantees of obligations which are drawn upon,] are automatically appropriated: Provided, that no obligations shall be incurred or payments made from funds thus automatically appropriatedexcept as issued in the form of regular budgetary allotments."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C065
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING THE OPEN HIGH SCHOOL SYSTEM IN THE PHILIPPINES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The open high school system delivers educational services to high school students utilizing print, radio, television and computer-based communications, satellite broadcasting, teleconferencin g and other multi-media learning and teaching technologies that allow students to study on their own without having to regularly attend classes in conventional classrooms. This alternative learning system is consistent with the constitutional mandate to democratize access to quality education at all levelseven as it "recognizes the vital role of the youth in nation-building ."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C012
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A NATIONAL SEAFARERS COMMISSION, PRESCRIBING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Through this proposed measure, the State shall institutionaliz e and redirect existing government efforts in effecting meaningful programs on the development, training, certification and welfare systems of local and overseas seafarers integrated under one agency.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C012
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING A SERVICE AREA SCHEME TO ALL INTERNET SERVICE PROVIDERS (ISPs) LIBERALIZING THE GRANTING OF ITS OPERATIONAL LICENSE TO OFFER EXPANDED SERVICES AND DEPLOY INTERNET BROADBAND INFRASTRUCTURE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The scheme will allow ISPs to render service in any area of their choice but will however, be required to operate a branch in at least one provincial area where there is an equal demand for Internet access. Granting this long time request of most ISPs to have their own network will also be beneficial to the country. By having a broadband network spread throughout the country, we can take advantage of the benefits the technology can deliver such as simultaneous and speedy transmission of multimedia signals between subscribers. Through this, our country will no longer be left out in the broadband race in the Asian region.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C012
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING VOLUNTEER FIRE ASSOCIATIONS FROM PAYMENT OF CUSTOMS TARIFFS AND DUTIES IN THE IMPORTATION OF FIRE TRUCKS AND SPARE PARTS THEREOF
rows.abstract: Fire trucks and spare parts consigned to volunteer fire associations shall be exempted from payment of import tax and duties. Volunteer fire associations shall refer to non profit, non government civic organizations duly registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission established for purposes of fire prevention and protection and rendering emergency medical assistance to fire victims which are accredited by the Bureau of Fire Protection.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C012
rows.title_full: AN ACT REORGANIZING AND MODERNIZING THE NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION AND PROVIDING NECESSARY FUNDS THEREFOR AND OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is hereby reorganized to meet the standards of an investigative and detective agency with expanded structure and manpower responsive to the demands of the times. The reorganized NBI shall be under the administrative supervision of the Department of Justice.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C012
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE COMMISSION ON ECONOMIC DIPLOMACY IN ORDER TO STRENGTHEN ECONOMIC DIPLOMACY AS A STRATEGY IN PHILIPPINE FOREIGN POLICY, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: With this proposal, the PHILIPPINE COMMISSION ON ECONOMIC DIPLOMACY (PCED) is established with the primary responsibility of developing and formulating policies and strategies on economic diplomacy and implementing them in order to generate foreignexchange and employment, project a good image of the country, and enhance the marketability of its products with support, assistance and cooperation of the local public and private sector, foreign governments and institutions and international traders.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOREIGN AFFAIRS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C012
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE FIELD OF LAND TITLE INSURANCE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 612, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE INSURANCE CODE OF 1978, AS AMENDED BY PRESIDENTIAL DECREES NO. 1455 AND 1460 AND BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 874
rows.abstract: Rationale: TITLE INSURANCE is a new field in this country, and there is a need for legislation to implement this and to encourage insurance companies to go into this venture. There is an urgency to implement title insurance as soon as possible, as title fraud has become a very serious problem. In order to implement a system of title insurance, there is a need to amend the Insurance Code of 1978 or PD 612 as amended, by adding the necessary provisions creating the field of title insurance.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS AND LIKEWISE INCREASING THE ALLOCATION FOR BARANGAYS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: This bill proposes to INCREASE the internal revenue allotment (IRA) allocated to local government units from [forty percent (40%)] to FORTY-FIVE PERCENT (45%), starting with the Fiscal Year 2003. The proposed increase of five percent (5%) shall allgo to the barangays which serve as the forefront of the delivery of essential public services.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09164) enacted on 2002-03-19
rows.title_full: AN ACT POSTPONING THE BARANGAY ELECTIONS FROM THE YEAR 2002 TO THE YEAR 2005 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The elections of barangay officials set for the Year 2002, as provided by law, is hereby POSTPONED and RESET to the second Monday of May, 2005, and the subsequent barangay elections shall be held every three (3) years thereafter.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04456

rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09164) enacted on 2002-03-19
rows.title_full: AN ACT POSTPONING THE ELECTIONS OF SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN OFFICIALS FROM THE YEAR 2002 TO THE YEAR 2005 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The elections of Sangguniang Kabataan officials set for the Year 2002, as provided by law, is hereby POSTPONED and RESET to the Year 2005, and the subsequent elections for the Sangguniang Kabataan shall be held every three (3) years thereafter.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04456

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE SOUTHERN PALAWAN ECONOMIC ZONE AND FREEPORT AUTHORITY (SPEZFA) IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF BALABAC IN PALAWAN,APPROPR IATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.status: Substituted by HB06422

rows.author: D045
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-12-17, transmitted to on 2003-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2004-01-06
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING VARIOUS FORMS OF UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICES AS ACTS OF ECONOMIC SABOTAGE, PRESCRIBING PENALTIES THEREFOR, GRANTING INCENTIVES AND REWARDS FOR ASSISTANCE OF WITNESSES AND INFORMANTS LEADING TO SUCCESSFUL PROSECUTION THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES (anti-trust)
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is hoped that this proposed measure be instrumental in curbing the proliferation of the activities of those engaged in unfair competition and trade practices that threaten the very foundation of the local industry and business sectorsin particular, and the Philippine economy, in general.  This Act likewise aims to ensure that the proper duties and taxes are paid to augment the government's depleted resources which are urgently needed to meet the society's basic requirements.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06530

first_reading.comm_act: change of ctte. ref'l from Justice as per J.5;p.30 (July 31,2001)

rows.author: B001
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE SPECIAL GROUP TERM INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR THE MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES, INCLUDING THE MEMBERS OF THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 352, AS AMENDED BY PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1965, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The members of the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the Philippine National Police, being primarily responsible for the preservation of peace, order and security of the country, are exposed to dangers of life and limb in their tasks ofsuppressing the activities of insurgents and lawless elements. The Special Group Term Insurance coverage of P12,000.00 is indeed very inadequate for the protection and security of the members and their families.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B001
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-09-03, transmitted to on 2002-09-03 and received by the Senate on 2002-09-03
rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE HOUSING SECTOR CREATING THEREBY THE DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT, DEFINING ITS STRUCTURE, PROVIDING FOR ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The proposed Department shall be primarily tasked with addressing the housing needs of the people, as well as land use and resettlement.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04517

rows.author: B001
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A ROAD DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: There is hereby created a body corporate to be known as "Road Development Authority", which shall be attached to the Office of President and charged primarily for the construction and/or rehabilitation, maintenance and operation of selected and desirable infrastructure projects that complement the overall national development efforts, where there are no takers from the private sector.  The principal office of the Authority shall be located in Metropolitan Manila, but it may establish offices elsewhere in the Philippines as may become necessary for the proper and efficient conduct of its business.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B001
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING RETIRED MEMBERS OF THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM THE FULL VALUE OF THEIR CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE SYSTEM, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8291, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM ACT OF 1997'
rows.abstract: The main objective of this bill is to grant the GSIS members who will retire from the service the total GSIS contributions of the member and the employer, including the interest earnings of the said contributions. To accomplish this objective, thisbill introduces the concept of "FULL VALUE OF CONTRIBUTIONS" which shall be used as the basis for the payment to the retirees of their lump sum and the basic monthly pension benefits which are likewise redefined in this Bill.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD AND VESTING IN IT THE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY OF ENFORCING MARITIME SAFETY RULES AND REGULATIONS AS WELL AS ANY OTHER MATTER RELATED TO THE PERFORMANCE OF SAFETY OF LIFE AND PROPERTY FUNCTIONS WITHIN PHILIPPINE TERRITORIAL WATERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Time and again, our inter-island vessels have been overloading on cargo and passengers, and this contributed to a number of sea tragedies. The tragedies notwithstanding , the overloading continues unabated because of greed for profits/money on the part of the shipping lines and the persons responsible for overseeing violations against loading capacities and limits. In the same manner, these inter-island vessels have been sailing without the necessary equipment and paraphernalia mandated by the safety of the vessels and their cargo passengers. Thus, this bill.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B015
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-07, transmitted to on 2002-05-09 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-13
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE PROHIBITED ACTS OF DISCRIMINATION AGAINST WOMEN ON ACCOUNT OF SEX, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 135 AND 137 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to ELIMINATE sex-based discrimination in employment by PENALIZING AN EMPLOYER WHO FAVORS A MALE EMPLOYEE OVER A FEMALE EMPLOYEE, WHETHER THROUGH NOTICES, ANNOUNCEMENTS OR ADVERTISEMENTS FOR EMPLOYMENT OR IN THE ACTUAL HIRING OR ADMISSION OF WORKERS.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04590

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER STRENGTHENING THE HOME DEVELOPMENT MUTUAL FUND AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Main thrusts of this proposed measure aimed at STRENGTHENING the PAG-IBIG FUND are as follows:  (1) Re-statement of the tax-exempt status of the Fund; (2) Provisions on FUND coverage, generation and contribution rates; (3) Power of the Board of Trustees as the ultimate policy determinant; (4) More teeth to the enforcement power of the FUND.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: change of ctte. ref'l from Housing and Urban Dev. as per J. 17; p.14(Aug. 28,2001)

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE FAKING OR FABRICATING, KNOWINGLY NEGOTIATING, TRANSACTING, CONVEYING OR MORTGAGING OF FAKE OR FABRICATED TORRENS CERTIFICATES OF TITLE A SPECIAL CRIME AND IMPOSING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The proposed bill seeks to provide the necessary deterrent to the proliferation of fake or fabricated titles by providing stiff penalties of fiftn (15) to thirty (30) years of imprisonment for faking and/or using spurious titles and classifying thesame as a heinous offense if committed bya syndicate or in large scale.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE NATIONAL POLICY ON, AND ESTABLISHING THE PROGRAM FRAMEWORK ON MENTAL HEALTH, PROVIDING THE IMPLEMENTING MECHANISMS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Largely, the medical and health care problems of the State have been successful. However, the State has yet to provide a program or to create a body that will address the problems attendant to the MENTAL HEALTH SITUATION.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 1 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BIG. 22, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ANTI-BOUNCING CHECKS LAW
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to INCREASE the penalties provided in BP Blg. 22 (Anti-Bouncing Check Law) to include, checks, made, drawn and issued by way of deposit or guarantee.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B015
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09225) enacted on 2003-08-29
rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING NATURAL-BORN CITIZENS OF THE PHILIPPINES WHO HAVE LOST THEIR CITIZENSHIP TO RETAIN CERTAIN RIGHTS AND PRIVILEGES RESERVED FOR FILIPINO CITIZENS
rows.abstract: Under this measure, former Philippine citizens may retain certain rights and privileges, such as: (1) operation of rural banks, registered overseas shipping; (2) engaging in retail trade, rice and corn indusatry, customs brokerage business; (3) practice of certain professions, etc.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04720

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR UNIFORM RETIREMENT BENEFITS FOR ALL GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES, PRESCRIBING PROCEDURES IN THE PROMPT PAYMENT THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: There is NO single law which governs the retirement of government officials and employees. Thus, retirement claims and benefits are embraced under several laws. One law covers the members of the Judiciary , another for the uniformed personnel of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, still another one deals with officials of the Constitutional bodies such as the Commission on Election, and still there is another law for the rest of the government workers. These laws, though providing two modes of retirement, optional and compulsory, provide DIFFERENT benefitical features and ages for retirement. Thus, the proposed bill is more in keeping with the principle of EQUITY and justice, for government personnel, whether on the top echelonn or a mere rank-and-file, are part of the government force who render service to the same institution with dedication, honesty and integrity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING HIGHER COMPENSATION TO VICTIMS OF UNJUST IMPRISONMENT OR DETENTION AND VICTIMS OF VIOLENT CRIMES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 4 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7309, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill provides that those who were unjustly imprisoned or detained for less than five (5) years shall be entitled to receive P1,000.00 for every month of such imprisonment. However, for those who where imprisoned for more than five (5) years areentitled to claim P2,000.00 for every month of such imprisonment or detention. While the compensation for the victims of violent crimes is increased from P10,000.00 to P100,000.00 considering the high cost of hospitalization and medical treatment.>The bill likewise, provides for psychiatric and medical treatment in any government hospital for those victims of unjust imprisonment and violent crimes for them to recover from their psychological or emotioal trauma.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B015
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09184) enacted on 2003-01-10
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MODERNIZATION, STANDARDIZATION AND REGULATION OF THE PROCUREMENT ACTIVITIES OF THE GOVERNMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This proposed measure seeks to promote basic principles in the procurement activities of the government, namely: (1) TRANSPARENCY; (2) ACCOUNTABILITY; EQUITY; (4) EFFECTIVENESS; (5) EFFICIENCY; and (6) ECONOMY.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04809

rows.author: B015
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09266) enacted on 2004-03-17
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MORE RESPONSIVE AND COMPREHENSIVE REGULATION FOR THE REGISTRATION, LICENSING AND PRACTICE OF ARCHITECTURE, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 545, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `AN ACT TO REGULATE THE PRACTICE OF ARCHITECTURE IN THE PHILIPPINES' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The State recognizes the importance of acrhitects in nation building and development. Hence, it shall develop and nurture competent, virtuous, productive and well-rounded professional architects whose standards of practice and service shall be exceelent, qualitative, world-class and globally competitive through inviolable, honest, effective and credible licensure examinations and through regulatory measures, programs and activities that foster their professional growth and development.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05389

first_reading.comm_act: chnge of cttee. ref'l from Revision of Laws as Per J.52; p.18

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO DEFINE AND PENALIZE CONSPIRACIES AND COMBINATIONS IN PUBLIC BIDDINGS, PREVENT ILLEGAL SCHEMES AND FRAUDS ENSURE FAIRNESS AND FREE COMPETITION, AND SAFEGUARD THE INTEREST OF THE GOVERNMENT
rows.abstract: "Competitive Public Bidding Act of 2001." This bill defines and penalizes conspiracies and combinations among public bidders.  It endeavors to protect the interest of the government, as well as public funds, by adopting appropriate measures to prevent illegal schemes, fraudulent acts, collusion, conspiracy, monopoly and unfair competition in public bidding process. It also relaxes the strict rules of evidence in order to make the prosecution of conniving bidders easier.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ADDITIONAL RETIREMENT BENEFITS TO MEMBERS OF THE JUDICIARY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 910, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The proposed bill aims to provide additional retirement benefits for members of the judiciary including the Court Administrator and the Deputy Court Administrators, by granting them, aside from their monthly salary, their HIGHEST aggregate of transportation, living and representation allownace during the residue of their natural lives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROCLAMATION OF ELECTED CANDIDATES WHEN NINETY PERCENT (90%) OF THE VOTES IN ANY PROVINCE, CITY OR MUNICIPALITY HAVE ALREADY BEEN CAST, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 6 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Experience shows that during the 1987, 1992 and 1995 elections, proclamation of elected Senators, Members of House of Representatives and local officials was marred with delays because of the failure of elections, particularly in some towns in Mindanao. The whole nation was held hostage to said special elections. Thus, this bill seeks to authorize the canvassing of returns and proclamation of winners of the electoral race when at least ninety percent of the votes in any province, city or municipality have already been cast. Under the measure, special elections shall no longer be called and the canvass and proclamation will proceed accordingly. This will greatly avert practice of candidated to engage in massive fraudulent and corrrupt activities to get votes from the remaining electorate.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-07-24

principal_referral.committee: MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS THIRTY-FOUR AND THIRTY-SIX, CHAPTER 12, TITLE III, BOOK IV OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The complexity and diversity of cases handled by the Office of the Solicitor General hone the legal minds and sharpen the skills of its lawyers in oral argumentation and writtem pleadings on any point of law. For the OSG to continuously maintain its image as painted by the highest court, itself, it is imperative that its structures be RATIONALIZED and UPGRADED.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING SPECIAL ASSISTANCE AND BENEFITS TO VOLUNTEER FIREMEN OF DULY RECOGNIZED FIRE BRIGADES OR CIVIC ORGANIZATIONS WHO DIE OR BECOME INCAPACITATED WHILE PROTECTING LIVES AND PROPERTIES DURING FIRES AND CONFLAGRATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to provide assitance and benefits to volunteer firefighters of duly recognized fire brigades and organizations, regardless of nationality, and members of barangay fire brigades trained by the Bureau of Fire Protection who are killedor incapacitated while in the line of duty in suppressing and protecting lives and properties from fires.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE SERVICE OF WARRANTS OF ARRESTS IN CERTAIN CASES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: Except only in cases of citizen's arrest of persons made as a result of surveillance and/or entrapment operations; persons being arrested for subversion and other crimes and offenses against national security; notorious and dangerous criminals for whom outstanding warrants of arrest have been issued; and escapist and fugitives from justice, it is hereby prohibited to serve warrants of arrests during nighttime, on legal holidays, or on weekends.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B015
rows.mother_status: House agreed on 2003-10-14 to the request for a conference made by the Senate on 2003-09-03
rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING A FARMER-BENEFICI ARY TO MORTGAGE HIS RIGHT TO THE LAND AWARDED TO HIM, FOR A PERIOD OF TWO (2) YEARS WITHOUT LOSING HIS SECURITY OF TENURE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION TWENTY-SEVEN OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-SIX HUNDRED ANDFIFTY-SEVEN, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `COMPREHENSIVE AGRARIAN REFORM LAW OF 1988,' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend Republic Act No. 6657 by allowing a farmer-benefici ary, who has not yet fully paid the value of the land awarded to him under the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program of the Government, to mortgage his rights thereto to any person within a period of not exceeding two (2) years. In order to ensure the farmer-benefici ary's capability to keep his right of ownership over his land and thus enchance the spirit of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Law, this bill provides that the farmer beneficiary shall NEITHER LOSE his security of tenure NOR BE EJECTED from the land, within the period of the mortgage, provided he regularly pays the amortization due to the Land Bank of the Philippines.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05511

rows.author: B015
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR AN EQUITABLE DISTRIBUTION OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT (IRA) TO, AND AUTHORIZING ITS AUTOMATIC RETENTION BY, THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 285 AND 286 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991', AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The share of local government units in the internal revenue allotment shall be allocated BEGINNING IN 1996, AFTER DEDUCTING THEREFROM THE FULL COSTS OF THE DEVOLVED FUNCTIONS AS WELL AS THE CITY FUNDED HOSPITALS, in the following manner: (a) Provinces - Twenty-three percent (23%); (b) Cities - Twenty-three percent (23%); (c) Municipalities - Thirty-four percent (34%); and (d) Barangays - Twenty-percent (20%) PROVIDED, HOWEVER, THAT IN THE EVENT THAT NEW CITIES ARE CREATED, THE EXISTING NUMBER OF CITIES PRIOR TO THE CREATION SHALL BE ALLOWED TO RECOVER THE AMOUNT OF NOT LESS THAN P899 MILLION EVERY YEAR WHICH THEY WOULD LOSE UNDER THE NEW ALLOCATION FORMULA AS PROVIDED IN THIS SECTION.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A GRANT OF REWARD TO INFORMERS OF VIOLATIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7080 AND/OR REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1379 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Any person, who voluntarily gives vital information supported by competent evidence not yet in possession of any government investigating agency, concerning ILL-GOTTEN WEALTH of any public official or employee, which materially accounted for or aided in the recovery of the said proeprty in favor of the State and/or the conviction of the guilty party in accordance with the provisions of Republic Act No. 7080 and/or Republic Act No. 1379, shall be entitled to a reward equivalent to twenty-five percentum (25%) of the value of the ill-gotten wealth actually collected or recovered.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 68 OF THE BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Any ELECTED OFFICIAL [candidate] who, in [an] A PROPER action or protest in which he is a party is declared by final decision of a competeent court guilty of, or found by the Commission of having (a) given money or other material consideration to influence, induce or corrupt the voters or public officials performing electoral functions; (b) committed acts of terrorism to enhance his candidacy; (c) spend in his election campaign an amount in excess of that allowed by this Code; (d) solicited, received or made any contribution prohibited under Sections 89, 95, 96, 97 and 104; or 15(e) violated of any Sections 80, 83, 85, 86 and 261 paragraphs d, e, k, v, and cc, sub-paragraph 6 (f) OR BEING A PERMANENT RESIDENT OR AN IMMIGRANT TO A FOREIGN CCOUNTRY REFUSED OR FAILED TO WAIVE HIS STATUS AS A PERMANENT RESIDENT OR AN IMMIGRANT TO A FOREIGN COUNTRY IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE RESIDENCE REQUIREMENT PROVIDED FOR IN THE ELECTION LAWS, shall be disqualified from holding the office.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE USE, MANUFACTURE, ACQUISITION, SALE AND DEPLOYMENT OF LANDMINES AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: It is the policy of the State to adhere to the international policy of working for the PROHIBITION or ABOLITION of weapons of mass destruction including those with indiscriminatel y, devastating or excessively injurious effects on civilian population. In pursuance of such policy, this Act prohibitis and restricts the use, manufacture, acquisition, sale and deployment of landmines.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INTEGRATING COOPERATIVE EDUCATION IN THE CURRICULUM OF TERTIARY EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS THROUGH PARTNERSHIP AMONG THE INSTITUTIONS, STUDENTS, BUSINESS, INDUSTRY AND AGRICULTURAL ENTITIES, AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR, ANDFOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to develop and maintain big caliber manpower in the Philippines by institutionaliz ing cooperative education as a unique structure educational strategy in tertiary education. It integrate classroom, study with paid, planned and supervised relevant works and paid experiences in the public and private sectors through partnership among the institution, the business and students, industry and agricultural entities with specified responsibility for each.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE MOVIE AND TELEVISION REVIEW AND CLASSIFICATION BOARD, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1986 `CREATING THE MOVIE AND TELEVISION REVIEW AND CLASSIFICATION BOARD,' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This proposed measure is premised on the following: (1) That it is the State policy to use media as a means of enforcing the law, protecting and promoting public morals and good customs, and NOT to corrupt the minds of the children and the youth; and (2) That the State warrants the self-regulation and policing of the movie, TV and cable TV industries.

rows.abstract: Rationale: The proposed REDUCTION in the income tax rates would strengthen the purchasing power of our people's hard-earned money in order to afford them the capability to meet the demands of daily living. In this light, not only do we hope to address the present financial difficulties of our taxpayers by increasing their take-home pay, but also to improve the country's economy by augmenting the current rate of consumption with the end view of enhancing economic activity.

rows.abstract: Rationale: The attached bill seeks to exempt senior citizens whose income is not more than One Hundred Twenty Thousand Pesos (P120,000.00) per annum, from the payment of real property tax and any tax on real property, such as the Special Education Fund Tax on their dwellings and the land on which it is situated, amending for the purpose Sections 2 and 4 of R.A. No. 7432, otherwise known as the Senior Citizens Law.> Senior citizens are now in the twilight years of their lives and most of them, having retired from work have no sufficient income to support their families with their daily needs, particularly at this time when prices of commodities have skyrocketed beyond the reach of minimum wage earners.

rows.abstract: ANY OFFICER OR EMPLOYEE OF THE LAND TRANSPORTATION OFFICE WHO IS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE REGISTATION OF A STOLEN VEHICLE SHALL BE PUNISHED BY A FINE EQUIVALENT TO THE MARKET VALUE OF THE STOLEN MOTOR VEHICLE REGISTERED OR IMPRISONMENT OF NOT LESS THAN ONE YEAR, OR BOTH, IN ADDITION THERETO, IF FOUND GUILTY, SUCH OFFICER OR EMPLOYEE SHALL BE DISMISSED FROM THE SERVICE WITH PREJUDICE TO REINSTATEMENT OR REEMPLOYEMENT IN THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE AND THAT ALL BENEFITS OR PRIVILEGES HE MAY BE ENTITLED SHALL BE FORFEITED.

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING EQUAL RIGHT TO WIVES AND HUSBAND, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 333, 334 AND 344 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: Rationale: Under the Revised Penal Code, Articles 333 and 334 define the felonies of adultery and concubinage, respectively. Their modes of committing are evidently different. The woman in an adultery case incurs a heavier penalty than the husband in a concubinage case. The marital infidelity of the husband is not treated as a felony unless the attendant circumstances in the felony of concubinage are present, creating therefore, a disadvantageous position on the part of the wife. Thus the needto amend Articles 333 and 334 of the Revised Penal Code to make the Code attuned to the fundamental equality before the law of women and men.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-24

rows.abstract: This bill proposes to INCREASE the minimum honoraria and allowances of barangay officials as follows: (1) [P1,000.00] P5,000.00 for the punong barangay; (2) [P600.00] P4,000.00 for each sangguniang barangay member, treasurer and secretary. Hospitalization benefits are likese INCREASED from [P5,000.00] to P7,000.00.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE RIGHT OF ACCESS TO INFORMATION ON MATTERS OF PUBLIC CONCERN GUARANTEED UNDER SECTION SEVEN, ARTICLE III OF THE 1987 CONSTITUTION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The following shall be made AVAILABLE for public scrutiny: records, documents, papers, research materials, tapes microfilm, videotapes and the like, statements of policy and interpretations thereof, final opinions, as well as orders made in the adjudication of cases, administative staff manuals and instructions affecting the public which are kept in or under the executive branch of the government, including the Office of the President, government research institutions, local governments, the military establishment and government-owne d or controlled-corp orations which are hereinafter referred to as government agencies.

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT LIMITING THE HOURS OF OPERATION OF NIGHTCLUBS, COCKTAIL LOUNGES, BARS AND SIMILAR ESTABLISHMENTS, AND PENALIZING THE VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Any provision of law, ordinance or regulation to the contrary, notwithstanding , no nightclub, cocktail lounge, bar or similar establishment serving liquor, wine or intoxicating drink, shall be OPENED for business earlier than 5:00 p.m. and later than 1:00 a.m.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE PAYMENT OF REAL PROPERTY TAXES AS A CONDITION PRIOR TO THE ISSUANCE OF BUILDING PERMIT OR CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION OF MACHINERY
rows.abstract: A local government unit, as an autonomous polical subdivision of the State, is now vested by law with more powers and increased responsibilitie s. However, a local government unit can not effectively carry out its functions and discharge its broadened powers on a wider scale without adequate resources. > As a collection strategy, therefore, this bill seeks to require all applicants for a building permit or a certificate of registration of machinery, etc. TO PAY FIRST the tax on the reap properties covered by the application before the building permit or certificate of registration shall be issued. The bill also provides penalties for violations thereof.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE RULES FOR A COMPETITIVELY NEUTRAL GOVERNMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "The Government Competitive Neutrality Act of 2001." Rationale: Undeniably, despite its pronounced policy of privatization and deregulation, the State continues to compete for available economic resources in the system. This has resulted in resourceallocation distortions which occur because prices charged by significant government businesses need not fully reflect resource costs. Thus, the need for competitive neutrality arrangements.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-24

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to regulate the business of producing and selling mineral, pure or distilled water. it also protects and safeguards the health of the citizens by insuring that the water they procure and consume are safe to drink as promoted and advertised by drinking water suppliers, distributors, or sellers.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY-SIX HUNDRED AND FIFTY-THREE, ENTITLED `THE NEW CENTRAL BANK ACT'
rows.abstract: The key provisions of this bill include: (1) the removal of the five-year time limit on the Bangko Sentral's tax exemption; (2) the granting of authority to the MOnetary Baord (MB) to provide a compensation structure based on job evaluation studiesand wage surveys, but not lower than those of any other government financial institutions;an d (3) the clarification that financial derivatives are subject to the regulation of the MB.

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT ENHANCING ECONOMIC COORDINATION, ADOPTING THE APPROPRIATE MECHANISM THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill is anchored on the dictum that economic goal setting should properly involve the Congress, the Governor and Monetary Board of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) as well as the National Economic Development Authority (NEDA) headed by the President. In the process, we may achieve better synchronization of monetary and fiscal policy or at least minimize the negative implications of their divergence. Moreover, it should similarly provide flesh to the mandate of accountability and transparency of the BSP.

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO FURTHER STRENGTHEN CONSUMER PROTECTION BY AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7394, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CONSUMER ACT OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to make NATIONAL CONSUMER AFFAIRS COUNCIL (NCAC) a truly independent body as intended by law. By placing it under the Office of the President, it shall have the power to: (1) prepare its annual budget for submission to the DBM; (2) create other positions as may be necessary in furtherance of its mandate; and (3) assume the authority to represent consumers in their claims and complaints invovlding violations of the Consumer Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT MODIFYING THE DEFINITION OF A CONDOMINIUM UNIT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4726, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CONDOMINIUM LAW TO APPLY TO INDUSTRIAL ESTATES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The bill seeks to amend R.A. 4726 to include the INDUSTRIAL ESTATES in the definition of the condominium. This bill gives investors more flexibility especially in planning in order them to maximize the use of space according to the needsof their operations. Also, the buildings and other structures within the industrial estates can be considered as collateral for loans and theregy improve the cash-flow position of firms.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REGULATION OF THE ORGANIZATION AND OPERATIONS OF INVESTMENT COMPANIES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Investment companies, which include mutual funds, contribute to the development of the capital market by pooling money from a large group of investors who have similar objectives. To strengthen the role of investment companies in the capital formation process, government needs to provide a favorable framework in which said companies can operate to facilitate the flow of investment capital and broaden participation in securities ownership by Filpinos.

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to expedite the administration of land registration proceedings paricularly in cases of loss or destruction of the original certificates of title in the custody of the Register of Deeds. > This bill also authorizes the Register  of Deeds to institute judicial action or to be deemed a party-in-intere st to a judicial action fore reconstitution of lost or destroyed original copy of a certificate of title being kept in his office.
